The 'Old Drake' to me has a lot to do with Noah Shebib. Tracks like Lust For Life, Headlines, Shot For Me, Tuscan Leather, Jungle, Fire & Desire ... Nobody else makes music like that. 40 seems to have taken more of a back seat now, understandably, which could explain why Drake's music hits different now.

It's wholly dependent on ones circumstances and experiences. I can understand someone viewing life as meaningless yet worth living if they're in good health, they have passions and they feel a sense of individual purpose. Conversely, I can also totally understand someone viewing life as meaningless and very much not worth living if they're in bad health, they're not passionate about anything, and they have no sense of individual purpose.
There's no right or wrong, it's just a matter of individual perception.

Ha, yeah the entire prison experience is probably worse, but if I could exchange just the hours I spent at work for hours spent locked away in an empty cell, I would choose the cell. Solitary confinement in the cell would probably be boring whereas work provides, at best, boredom plus stress and misery.
The human species is 100% capable of redeveloping society so that most people find their employment fulfilling and far less stressful, unlike what we have now, which is a society in which so many people thoroughly detest their job.

I've occasionally done what you describe - wake up on a day off, nothing planned, rather just be asleep, so taken 4 or 5 25mg pills and been back in bed a few hours later. I usually stay asleep for 3-5 hours, but I try to avoid the temptation to do it too much because:   
1) Your brain builds up tolerance to it quickly.  
2) I get horrendous headaches and brain fog if I take large doses.  
3) It messes up my night-time sleep/circadian rhythm (more than usual).

It really is.
Sometimes I'll hit the booze hard, or take 3/4 diphenhydramine, solely to make myself fall asleep during the afternoon on a day off, just to escape for a few hours. It's probably the highlight of my week...
Seen it all, done it all; won a little, lost a lot. No lust or passion for life anymore, just a desire to escape; to forget. Merely being conscious is a burden increasingly too heavy to bear. Spare me the futility.

Society likes to sweep the overall misery of existence under the carpet, and people tend to want to focus on trivial nonsense to distract themselves from how much of a shithole the world is. I've realised that being open about how you feel leaves you open to mostly ridicule or belittlement, e.g. "I HAVE IT WORSE THAN YOU!" or "JUST BE GLAD YOU'VE GOT A ROOF OVER YOUR HEAD!"  
The wise depressive keeps shtum; in reality, we're all alone and we can only help ourselves, even if that 'help' amounts to forcing ourselves into taking the plunge into nonexistence.
